title: Boolean Blindness (Flag Arguments)
pattern: A function signature accepting multiple raw boolean parameters to toggle different execution paths or behaviors.
why_bad: Call sites are completely unreadable and highly error-prone. A developer reading `configure_server("localhost", true, false, true)` has no idea what each flag controls without jumping to the function definition, and can easily swap boolean arguments with zero compiler warnings.
detection: Look for functions that accept 2 or more boolean arguments, particularly when they are passed as raw literals at the call sites.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Standard library methods or internal private helpers where only a single boolean flag is passed, although explicit enums are still safer.
fix: Replace the boolean parameters with descriptive, single-variant or multi-variant `enum`s.
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 10, "Replace Parameter with Explicit Methods"; *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 7; *Scott Wlaschin - Domain Modeling Made Functional (2017)*.
